We use relative clauses to give more information about what we are talking about, so that it can be clear.
We were talking about some important aspects of databases that you have to take into account for our next exam.
If you had more knowledge about ASP.NET, we would be able to cover other .NET tools whose objective is to let programmers access data, such as SqlDataSource.

Within relative clauses, there are subject and object relative clauses.

You use relative pronouns to give more information about what you're talking about. Those relative pronouns are: who – which – that.

Relative Clauses - Subject
You use them to clarify something and you use them after the subject.

Example:
I was looking for the programmer who can control databases well.
She was looking for someone that can help her.

Relative Clause - Object
You use them to clarify something or to give extra information about objects or situations.

Example:
Kevin deals with databases which are hard to control.
Kevin work on database that are tough to control.
You use unreal conditional sentences to describe how a person or system would react in a hypothetical situation, which will hardly take place in the real world.

In fact, if you had the chance to handle and know about ASP.NET, you would definitely discover that it is useful to perform different actions like working with XML documents, flat files, and business objects, among others.
If I had more time before this class ends, I would give you more details about important aspects of database access.

In English you use the second conditional to speak about present and future situations which are unlikely to happen.

This second conditional follows a specific grammatical structure using the simple past and would. Check the structure that we use.

images.text: <div align="justify">We were talking about some important aspects of databases that you have to take into account for our next exam. Think about the following question: If you had the chance to access a data, how would you do it? Well, I am pretty sure that many of you would definitely use the ASP.NET tool to do so. In fact, if you had the chance to handle and know about ASP.NET, you would definitely discover that it is useful to perform different actions like working with XML documents, flat files, and business objects, among others. If you asked any programmer why ASP.NET is so important, he would tell you that it actually hides all the complex processes of data access and makes it easier to access data; plus, it connects different ASP.NET control objects and the backend data source. </br>

<div align="justify">Data controls, which are vital for the database content retrieval, use ASP.NET. First of all, we have the data source control, that manages the connection to the data as well as its selection. In fact, it is the one that pages and caches the data. </br>

<div align="justify">On the other hand, we have the data view control, which drags and displays the data so it can be manipulated. If you had more knowledge about ASP.NET, we would be able to cover other .NET tools whose objective is to let programmers access data, such as SqlDataSource, or GridView to manipulate it. Oh, oh I am afraid time is up. If I had more time before this class ends, I would give you more details about important aspects of database access.

Instructions:

1. Write a descriptive text about database access in ASP.NET.
2. Start your descriptive text with an introduction paragraph in which you introduce the concept as well as the structure of the rest of the text.
3. Then, write a paragraph explaining how to access databases using ASP.NET.
4. Write three or more steps explaining this process using the second conditional.
5. Finally, introduce a concluding paragraph in which you sum up the ideas you exposed.

When you have typed in ALL your answers, click the Go to Writing Task button.

When you are writing remember:

1. An introductory paragraph.
2. Remember to use technical vocabulary.
3. The description of the process divided in three steps.
4. Make sure that you wrote a comprehensible text that is easy to read and understand.
